title: A blur you add to a box actually softens it
goal: Add a blur to a rectangle and nothing happens: the box looks exactly as it did. On an ellipse the blur works but its soft halo is cut off square at the edge of the shape, so a blurred circle sits in an invisible box. A blur should soften the shape and spread past its edge the way a shadow does.
notes:
Reproduced on the probe on 2026-09-07 while finishing removing-or-switching-off-an-effect-is-remembere. Two walks, each drawing a shape, rendering the document, adding a Blur from the Effects plus, and rendering again:

  Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/pz/blurcheck.json    (rectangle)
  Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/pz/blurcheck2.json   (arrow, then ellipse)

Comparing the two renders with PIL:
  rectangle before -> after diff bbox: None          (nothing changed at all)
  arrow     before -> after diff bbox: (84, 84, 316, 266)   (paints, and spreads past the drawn line)
  ellipse   before -> after diff bbox: (350, 100, 500, 250) (exactly the drag box: the halo is cut off)

The walk also asserted the panel agrees the blur is on (expect control Switch in Blur reads "Blur, on"), so this is the renderer and not the model.

Diagnosis: DocumentRenderer.swift:777 does image = blurred(image, radius: layer.style.blurRadius) on the layer raster, and blurred() clamps to the extent before blurring so the edges do not fade to transparent. A rectangle annotation raster is solid edge to edge, so clamp + blur + crop back to the same extent returns the identical image. The layer needs room around it before the blur, the way LayerStyle.padding (Layer.swift:972, blurRadius * 3) already implies, and the crop afterwards has to keep that room.
acceptance: Adding a blur to a rectangle visibly softens it, edges and all
A blurred ellipse fades out in every direction instead of being cut off square
Turning the blur off puts the shape back exactly as it was
Every other shape that already blurs (arrows, lines) keeps doing it
